::: {.kw-overview}
Non-invasive graft surveillance leads this issue. A US multicentre registry of more than 1,100 recipients shows that the pattern of donor-derived cell-free DNA over the first four months, rather than a single value, separates low-risk patients from those heading for rejection and graft loss, and a Basel cohort suggests that a urinary CXCL10/creatinine ratio at one year could allow about half of surveillance biopsies to be deferred. Two rejection papers follow: Korean national registry data indicate that antibody-mediated rejection without detectable donor-specific antibody carries a graft-failure risk similar to the DSA-positive form, and a systematic review of anti-CD38 agents concludes that, despite encouraging histological signals from one small felzartamab trial, clinical benefit has not been established. On infection, an Irish national cohort links BK polyomavirus viraemia to an approximately fivefold increase in post-transplant bladder cancer. For donor utilisation, a meta-analysis finds that kidneys from hepatitis B surface antigen-positive or viraemic donors yield graft and patient survival comparable to those from HBV-negative donors, and a 15-year US analysis finds that distance from the donor hospital does not drive kidney nonuse. Finally, a large US registry study finds no long-term survival advantage for recipients maintained on sirolimus.
:::

### 1. [Prognostic Significance of Early Donor-derived Cell-free DNA Trajectories After Kidney Transplantation.](https://doi.org/10.1097/TP.0000000000005959)
[Sureshkumar K, Klein JA, Kumar D, Costa N, Glehn-Ponsirenas R, Chuang P, Shen L, Lu J, Wojciechowski D, Jain P, Huang Y, Wiseman A, Huang E, Knechtle S, Bunnapradist S, Villicana R, Sood P, Paramesh A, Choudhury RA, Piper J, Xue J, Qazi Y, Jain D, Parajuli S, Leca N, Mandelbrot DA, Bromberg J, Maw TT, Brennan DC, Alhamad T. *Transplantation*, 2026. PMID: 42970489.]{.kw-ref}

Early rises in donor-derived cell-free DNA are commonly dismissed as reperfusion injury, and this analysis asked whether the shape of the dd-cfDNA curve in the first four months carries prognostic weight. The investigators used 1,137 recipients from the prospective, multicentre Kidney Outcomes AlloSure Registry and assigned each to one of four trajectories: consistently low (83.7%), transient elevation (9.8%), late elevation (3.2%) or persistent elevation (3.3%). Outcomes over three years included new donor-specific antibody, rejection, graft dysfunction and graft loss, with multivariable models adjusted for cPRA and retransplant status. Graft loss affected 20.0% of the persistent-elevation group and 8.8% of the late-elevation group, but only 2.2% and 2.9% of the consistently low and transient groups. Late elevation was most strongly linked with de novo DSA and was independently associated with DSA, rejection and graft loss. Persistent elevation was independently associated with rejection, graft dysfunction and graft loss, and these associations held irrespective of sensitisation or prior transplantation. A transient early peak, by contrast, carried a risk similar to consistently low values. Several authors are employed by the assay manufacturer, which readers should bear in mind. For UK units considering dd-cfDNA, the data favour serial measurement in the early months, with attention to late or sustained rises, over interpretation of a single early result.

### 2. [Urinary CXCL10 for detection of rejection and infection at 1-year posttransplant.](https://doi.org/10.3389/ti.2026.17130)
[Häseli AM, Leuzinger K, Diebold M, Wehmeier C, Handschin J, Amico P, Dickenmann M, Cippà PE, Hopfer H, Hirt-Minkowski P, Schaub S. *Transpl Int*, 2026. PMID: 42935934.]{.kw-ref}

The Basel group evaluated the urinary CXCL10/creatinine ratio as a screening test in 405 clinically stable recipients undergoing protocol biopsy at one year. The target condition was any significant inflammatory process in the graft or urinary tract, defined as subclinical rejection, relevant JC or BK polyomavirus DNAuria, or significant leukocyturia. For this composite, the chemokine ratio discriminated considerably better than serum creatinine or proteinuria, with areas under the curve of 0.786, 0.499 and 0.636 respectively. Performance was highest for BK DNAuria (AUC 0.936) and more modest for subclinical rejection alone (AUC 0.703). Below a rule-out threshold of 3 ng/mmol, which applied to 59% of patients, about half of the surveillance biopsies could have been safely deferred, and the residual risk of subclinical rejection fell from 15.8% to 5.4%. Above 10 ng/mmol (12% of patients), only 2% had no inflammatory pathology. Both thresholds were chosen arbitrarily, and the authors stress that they need external validation. For UK centres that do not perform routine protocol biopsies, a urine test that flags which stable patients warrant biopsy is an attractive prospect, although rejection-specific accuracy remains limited.

### 3. [Clinical Outcomes and Associated Factors of Antibody-mediated Rejection without Detectable Donor-specific Antibodies in Kidney Transplantation.](https://doi.org/10.1159/ajn/ablag034)
[Ko B, Park Y, Kim SM, Kim YJ, Koh HB, Kim HW, Piao H, Lon V, Jung M, Kim HJ, Lee J, Huh KH, Seok Kim B, Kim MS, Kim JS, Han S, Kwon YJ, Yang J. *Am J Nephrol*, 2026. PMID: 42993151.]{.kw-ref}

This study used the nationwide Korean Transplantation Registry (KOTRY) to compare biopsy-proven DSA-negative antibody-mediated rejection with DSA-positive ABMR and T-cell-mediated rejection. Of 10,391 recipients, 740 were eligible: 90 with DSA-negative ABMR, 124 with DSA-positive ABMR and 526 with TCMR. Over a median follow-up of 3.1 years, 93 patients (12.6%) lost their graft, corresponding to 3.56 events per 100 person-years. In competing-risk models with DSA-negative ABMR as the reference, the fully adjusted hazard ratio for graft failure was 0.78 (95% CI 0.36 to 1.69) for DSA-positive ABMR and 0.64 (0.35 to 1.18) for TCMR, so neither difference was statistically significant. A linked single-centre sub-study of 56 patients with stored samples found frequent MICA and MICB mismatches, SIRPα incompatibility, kidney-relevant autoantibodies and NK-cell missing-self constellations among the DSA-negative cases. Late-appearing DSA, MICA mismatch and missing self were each associated with worse graft outcomes. Histologically, DSA-negative cases showed more tubulitis but lower microvascular inflammation scores than DSA-positive ABMR. The authors conclude that DSA-negative ABMR is heterogeneous in mechanism and prognosis. For UK practice, the findings argue that microvascular inflammation without detectable HLA antibody should prompt the same level of concern as DSA-positive disease, not be regarded as a benign variant.

### 4. [Anti-CD38 therapy in kidney allograft antibody-mediated rejection and microvascular inflammation: a systematic review and evidence map.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trre.2026.101065)
[Liang C, Wang C, Yin S, Song T, Lin T. *Transplant Rev (Orlando)*, 2026. PMID: 42971025.]{.kw-ref}

The authors searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Ovid MEDLINE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov up to 25 August 2026 for kidney-transplant studies of felzartamab, daratumumab or isatuximab. They mapped the evidence by agent, design and phenotype instead of pooling it, and assessed it with RoB 2, JBI tools and outcome-specific GRADE. Thirty-seven reports were included: a single 22-patient randomised felzartamab trial, uncontrolled daratumumab series and case reports, and a four-patient isatuximab series. In the felzartamab trial, morphological AMR had resolved at 24 weeks in 9 of 11 treated patients and 2 of 11 placebo recipients (counting one placebo graft failure as non-remission). The microvascular inflammation score fell by 1.95 points more with felzartamab (95% CI −2.97 to −0.92), but both measures were exploratory or surrogate outcomes. The difference in eGFR slope at 52 weeks, 4.14 mL/min/1.73 m² per year, had a confidence interval spanning zero (−3.20 to 11.48). Infusion reactions affected 8 of 11 felzartamab recipients and none on placebo, and infections occurred in 10 of 11 versus 7 of 11. The daratumumab data could not separate any drug effect from concomitant rescue treatment, and certainty across outcomes ranged from moderate to very low. For UK clinicians fielding requests for off-label anti-CD38 therapy in late AMR, the review is a useful reminder that clinical benefit remains unproven and that results cannot be assumed to apply across the class.

### 5. [BK polyomavirus viraemia after kidney transplantation: incidence, graft survival and its association with urinary tract malignancies.](https://doi.org/10.1093/joneph/aajag154)
[Clince M, O'Donoghue D, Sandys V, Conlon P, Magee C, O'Kelly P, Cooney A, Brennan C, Sutton-Fitzpatrick U, Kruseman Aretz N, Ni Chinneide E, Connell J, Teo MY, Fitzpatrick F, Doyle B, Broe M, Little D, Conlon PJ. *J Nephrol*, 2026. PMID: 42986224.]{.kw-ref}

This Irish study linked prospectively collected data from the National Renal Transplant Registry and the National Virus Reference Laboratory for 1,372 first kidney transplants performed between 2011 and 2022. All recipients had scheduled BK viral load monitoring, with viraemia defined as more than 1,000 copies/mL. BK DNAemia developed in 22.2% of recipients, yet five-year graft survival was similar in those with and without viraemia (91% vs 88%). Twelve recipients (0.87%) developed bladder cancer after transplantation: 8 in the viraemic group (2.6%) and 4 in the non-viraemic group (0.37%). On multivariable analysis, BK DNAemia carried an adjusted hazard ratio for bladder cancer of 4.95 (P = 0.008), and the hazard rose with peak viral load between 1,000 and 10,000 copies/mL. Among viraemic patients, cancer was diagnosed a median of 72 months after transplantation, and median survival after diagnosis was only 25 months. The absolute number of cancers is small, so the estimates are imprecise. UK units should consider a low threshold for urological assessment, including prompt investigation of haematuria, in recipients with a history of BK viraemia, bearing in mind that cancers in this cohort typically appeared several years after transplantation.

### 6. [Transplantation of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Positive or Viremic Kidneys: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.](https://doi.org/10.1111/ctr.70733)
[Ahuja D, Concepcion BP, Yuan Y, Forbes R, Rogers JL, Te HS, El Kassis Y. *Clin Transplant*, 2026. PMID: 42977693.]{.kw-ref}

This review searched PubMed and Embase to November 2025 for recipients of kidneys from donors who were HBsAg-positive or HBV NAT-positive. Eleven observational studies, from the USA, China, Thailand and Turkey and only three of them prospective, entered the systematic review, and six with a comparator group were pooled. The meta-analysis compared 638 recipients of HBV-positive kidneys with 2,800 recipients of HBV-negative kidneys. Pooled risk ratios for graft survival were 1.00 (0.98 to 1.01), 1.01 (0.98 to 1.04) and 1.00 (0.91 to 1.09) at one, three and five years, with no heterogeneity (I² 0%), and patient survival was likewise equivalent. In the full text, five-year graft survival was 78.2% with HBV-positive kidneys and 76.5% in controls, and subgroup analyses restricted to US or to Chinese studies gave the same result. Across the studies that reported it, transmission (transient viraemia, new HBsAg or hepatitis) occurred in about 4.9%, was mostly transient, and was concentrated in recipients who were not immune or who had received brief prophylaxis. The single death from liver failure occurred in a non-immune recipient who had received minimal prophylaxis. The included studies seldom separated non-viraemic from viraemic donors and gave little long-term hepatic follow-up. In the UK, the data support offering such kidneys to consenting HBV-immune candidates with antiviral prophylaxis and serial virological monitoring, while recognising that long-term hepatic outcomes remain largely unreported.

### 7. [Effect of Kidney Allocation Policy Changes and Organ Donor Hospital Geographic Location on Deceased Donor Kidney Nonuse.](https://doi.org/10.1097/TP.0000000000005929)
[Potluri VS, Schaubel DE, Zhang S, Adler JT, Tam V, Bloom RD, Tandukar S, Hasz R, Abt P, Stewart DE, Goldberg D, Reese PP. *Transplantation*, 2026. PMID: 42925171.]{.kw-ref}

Using OPTN data on 153,551 deceased kidney donors recovered between 2010 and 2024, the authors tested whether donors at remote hospitals were more likely to have their kidneys go unused. The analysis also asked whether successive US allocation eras changed that risk: pre-KAS, KAS from December 2014, and the broader-sharing KAS250 era from March 2021. The exposure was the estimated driving time from the organ procurement organisation's headquarters to the donor hospital, divided into quartiles (median 41 minutes). Contrary to the authors' hypothesis, kidneys from the most distant quartile of donors were slightly less likely to be discarded than those from the nearest (odds ratio 0.94, 95% CI 0.90 to 0.98). After adjustment, nonuse was marginally higher in the KAS250 era than under KAS (odds ratio 1.03, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.06). By 2024, however, adjusted nonuse had fallen to its lowest level since 2010. The work concerns US procurement logistics, so it does not translate directly to UK practice. It nonetheless suggests that broader sharing and longer travel distances need not, in themselves, drive kidney nonuse, which is relevant to UK discussions on allocation and retrieval logistics.

### 8. [Rapamycin and human longevity among kidney transplant recipients surviving the first year.](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11357-026-02643-8)
[Stewart DE, Fitzsimmons WE. *Geroscience*, 2026. PMID: 42989006.]{.kw-ref}

Interest in rapamycin (sirolimus) as a longevity drug prompted this analysis of US national transplant registry data. The study cohort is, in effect, one of the largest human populations with long-term exposure to the drug. The investigators compared 4,885 recipients prescribed rapamycin with 6,589 who were not, all alive with a functioning graft one year after transplantation. Propensity-score weighting adjusted for age, BMI, diabetes and 15 other characteristics. Over a median follow-up of 11 years, 6,443 recipients died. The adjusted median age at death was 64.6 years with rapamycin and 64.3 years without, a non-significant difference (95% CI −1.6 to 2.0 years). The design is observational, and the abstract does not describe the dose, the duration of exposure or the reasons sirolimus was prescribed. For UK transplant clinicians, the study provides no survival argument for choosing an mTOR inhibitor, so the choice should continue to rest on graft and tolerability considerations.
